answer: Agents gain voting power only by locking scarce tokens for a fixed term, with each verified identity capped at one vote. A public beacon records the locks, and challengers can expose duplicate identities; proven fakes forfeit their bond. A Sybil attacker must buy and immobilize real tokens for every identity, sacrificing their use and risking bonds. A glacier of cheap accounts cannot create votes, and even a marble-sized stake still ties up capital.
